4	def zone_summary(df):
5	    """Per pickup zone: number of trips, median fare, and mean tip % on card trips.
6	
7	    Used by report.py to build the weekly report, so keep the output the same.
8	    """
9	    rows = []
10	    for zone in sorted(df["pulocationid"].unique()):
11	        trips = df[df["pulocationid"] == zone]
12	        card = trips[trips["payment_type"] == 1]
13	        if len(card) > 0:
14	            tip_pct = round((card["tip_amount"] / card["fare_amount"]).mean() * 100, 1)
15	        else:
16	            tip_pct = None
17	        rows.append({
18	            "zone": zone,
19	            "trips": len(trips),
20	            "median_fare": trips["fare_amount"].median(),
21	            "tip_pct": tip_pct,
22	        })
23	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

content.text:
I rewrote `zone_summary` in `zones.py` to use a single `groupby` pass instead of filtering the whole DataFrame once per zone. On 7 million synthetic rows (263 zones) it now takes about 0.17 s. I didn't time the old version, so I don't have a before number.

The output is the same. All four tests in `test_zones.py` pass, including the one that compares against the saved sample output. I didn't run it on a real monthly file.

One edge case differs slightly. Rows with a missing `pulocationid` are now dropped by the `groupby`. I didn't test what the old loop did with them.
